content:
The image shows two soybean stems close-up. Key visual features:

- **Small black specks** densely covering the stem surfaces
- The specks appear scattered randomly across the stem (not in linear rows)
- Stem tissue appears grayish, bleached, and dry
- No white fluffy mold, no sclerotia embedded in white mycelium
- The black specks are beneath/on the epidermis, giving a "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance
- Stems appear desiccated with reddish-brown undertones visible

This matches **Charcoal Rot** very well: microsclerotia (small black specks) scattered beneath the epidermis of the lower stem, giving the characteristic charcoal-sprinkled appearance on a grayish stem.

Differentiating from alternatives:
- **Diaporthe/Pod & Stem Blight**: pycnidia appear in linear rows — these specks are randomly scattered
- **White Mold**: would show fluffy white mycelium and large black sclerotia — not present
- **Anthracnose**: acervuli with setae on stems/pods, typically darker irregular lesions — different pattern
